title: the Palatinate Rising
premise: In 1849, in a print shop in the Rhenish Palatinate, Paloma Voss hides her late father's forbidden typeface and her own talent for cutting letters while revolution gathers in the streets. When an infant is abandoned at the shop's door with a note naming her dead father as the boy's kin, Paloma discovers the child is heir to both her family's press and a fortune her uncle will kill to claim. As Prussian troops close in, she must smuggle the boy — and the truth of his inheritance — out on the last river barge, choosing between saving her found family of printers or keeping the berth for herself. In the end she gives up her place, stays behind to print one final seditious broadside, and wins a new kind of belonging: the town that once overlooked her now carries her name in every line they set.
about_author: Quentin Thackeray is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in workshops across the Rhineland. The Palatinate Rising is a debut novel drawn from family letters discovered in a Heidelberg bindery.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In the Voss print shop, Paloma secretly cuts type at night while her surrogate family of printers debates the coming uprising. A bundle appears at the door: an infant, a note, and a seal bearing her father's mark. Emotional beat: quiet longing cracked open by sudden responsibility.

chapters.title: Ink and Blood Kin
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Paloma and Uncle Anselm, who arrives claiming the child and the press. Paloma uncovers letters proving the boy is her half-brother and heir to the Voss estate. Rising tension: Anselm's men search the shop; the printers close ranks around her. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into fierce loyalty.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Climax. With Prussian troops entering the city, the printers plan escape by river barge, but there is only one berth left among them for the child's guardian. Anselm corners Paloma at the dock; a firefight erupts amid the presses being loaded. She must choose who boards. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Every Line They Set
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, months later. Having given her berth to the child and old master printer Grett, she remains, printing the republic's first legal broadside after the garrison falls. The boy returns with Grett to a shop reborn under her name. Emotional beat: grief resolved into earned belonging and found family made permanent.
